content.comment_body: I'm a macOS user and have used [product_name] on macOS for many years without any problems, especially with HiDPI screens using Java. After switching to a new Lenovo laptop with an OLED 2880x1800 display at 243 PPI, Windows 11 scaled the screen to 200%. This setup does not work smoothly with [product_name] [version_no] and AWS Corretto Java version 11. First, I tried setting the software scaling to 150%, which improved things slightly but the text was still tiny. In Windows 11, under the compatibility tab, if you right-click javaw.exe in the jre folder and open properties, you can adjust high DPI settings. Here, you can enable high DPI scaling override and set it to either 'system' or 'system enhanced.' After researching online about Java support for HiDPI displays, I found the option: Dsun.java2d.uiScale.enabled=true, but have not tested it with AWS Corretto 11 yet. For now, setting the application scaling to 100% makes it resemble the MacBook Pro 14 experience. I hope these tips help others trying to use [product_name] on an OLED HiDPI display with Microsoft Windows 11.

analysis.insight_summary: Users switching from macOS to Windows 11 with a HiDPI OLED display encounter usability issues with [product_name] [version_no], mainly small and hard-to-read text due to scaling problems on high-resolution screens. Adjusting both OS and app scaling helps but still requires several manual tweaks to improve readability.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] to function smoothly with HiDPI/OLED screens on Windows 11, offering readable interfaces similar to the macOS experience without needing additional compatibility or scaling adjustments.
